root_cause: The elision logic conflated numeric value-equivalence (proven by TryGetInt32Constant/Smi::IsValid) with Smi tagging. For non-tagged representations the two are equivalent because the fallback switch performs an explicit value-range check; but for kTagged inputs the fallback check (CheckSmi) verifies the pointer's tag bits, a distinct property not implied by numeric equivalence, especially since the 'checked_value' alternative can be populated with a HeapNumber constant purely from a same-value float comparison.
findings: MaglevGraphBuilder::BuildCheckSmi() added an optimization that skips emitting the runtime Smi check whenever TryGetInt32Constant(object) returns a value that lies within the Smi range (Smi::IsValid).
